h1:
Fiery Southern Food in Trang
Gaeng Tai Pla, Khua Kling & Stink Bean
intro: Trang is famous for its roast pork and dim sum, sure — but ask a local what they had for lunch and the answer is usually a plate of bold Southern rice-curry: fragrant khua kling, a rich, salty gaeng tai pla, and stink-bean stir-fry that smells strong but wins you over. These are the Southern Thai spots in Trang that locals actually eat at, picked from real reviews and places still open today.

blocks.html: Southern food in Trang stands out for its heavy-handed curry paste — loads of turmeric, fresh chillies, and the salty kick of shrimp paste that no Southerner cooks without. First-timers from outside the region sometimes flinch because it runs hotter than they expect, but once it grabs you, plain food never tastes the same again. We've split this into the dishes you should try first, then the spots locals genuinely go to — both rice-curry shops and made-to-order kitchens.

blocks.text: Three main dishes you have to try

items.name: Gaeng Tai Pla (fish-kidney curry)
items.blurb: The most intense curry in the Southern playbook, built on tai pla (fermented, salted fish innards), with grilled fish, bamboo shoots, eggplant and pumpkin. Eaten with raw veg on the side to cut the punch. It's the dish that tests newcomers — but get past it and you'll understand why Southerners love it.
items.meta: Very spicy, salt-forward · eaten with rice and fresh veg

items.name: Khua Kling
items.blurb: Minced pork or beef dry-fried with Southern curry paste until it's almost crisp, fragrant with paste and shredded kaffir lime leaf, with a heat that goes straight up your nose. Locals eat it with hot steamed rice, and you'll find it at nearly every rice-curry shop and made-to-order kitchen.

items.name: Stink Bean Stir-fry with Fresh Shrimp
items.blurb: Stink beans (sator) stir-fried with shrimp paste and fresh shrimp — the strong smell is part of the charm. The salty-sweet shrimp paste plays off the richness of the shrimp, and you can order it with rice-curry just about anywhere. For locals, it's an everyday plate.

items.name: Gaeng Lueang (Southern sour curry)
items.blurb: A sour-and-spicy yellow curry coloured by turmeric, usually made with mullet, queenfish or pickled bamboo shoots. Far bolder than the central-Thai version of sour curry, and a plate locals in Trang almost always order alongside khua kling.
items.meta: Sour, spicy, heavy on turmeric · from ฿80–180

items.name: Pak Liang Stir-fried with Egg
items.blurb: Pak liang, a Southern wild vegetable, stir-fried with egg — soft and mellow, the palate-rester after you've eaten a run of fiery dishes. Pretty much every Southern restaurant in Trang has it.

blocks.title: Surviving the heat
blocks.html: If you're not used to Southern food, you can ask for it mild, and always order pak noah (fresh veg on the side) to cut the heat. As for gaeng tai pla, share a portion to taste first — it's the boldest dish of the lot.

blocks.text: Southern rice-curry shops where locals eat lunch

blocks.html: Lunch for a lot of people in Trang means a rice-curry shop with a row of trays to point at — cheap, and you get several things on one plate. These are the places where you'll find gaeng tai pla, khua kling and gaeng lueang all in one spot, cooked the traditional way.

items.name: Krua Khon Trang
items.blurb: A Southern kitchen locals bring up often. The standouts are dry-fried soft pork ribs, pork khua kling, and a bold gaeng tai pla. This is real Southern flavour, not toned down for outsiders.
items.meta: Central Trang (Thap Thiang) · authentic Southern flavour

items.name: Sifa Lifestyle Food
items.blurb: A spot on Phatthalung Road in the Thap Thiang area serving Southern curries, rice porridge, kao yok (braised pork belly), sour curry with acacia and egg, and shrimp with stink bean. Relaxed setting, good for anyone who wants Southern food without diving into a full-on rice-curry shop.

items.name: Jeen Dam (Huai Yot)
items.blurb: An old shop in the Huai Yot area on Phetkasem Road, known for crab spring rolls, Trang-style kao yok, and shrimp stir-fried with shrimp paste and stink bean. Worth a stop if you're passing through Huai Yot toward Thap Thiang.
items.meta: Phetkasem Rd, Huai Yot · open 11:00–20:30 (closed Sat)

items.name: Krua Thong Na Tham
items.blurb: A home-style place out of town in the Na Tham area, known for mullet gaeng lueang, shrimp with stink bean, pak liang stir-fried with egg, and garlic-fried squid. Flavours that aren't over the top, and easy on the wallet.

items.name: Ko Choi
items.blurb: An old in-town shop that's been going for decades. The picks are shrimp stir-fried with shrimp paste and stink bean, pak liang with egg, and a lineup of bold Southern dishes. Older locals in Trang still come here regularly.

items.name: Krua Mueang Trang
items.blurb: A shop reviewers praise for flavours that go heavy on the spices. Strong on mixed-veg gaeng lueang with shrimp, and stink bean with shrimp stir-fried in shrimp paste. Good for anyone who wants deep Southern flavour with no dialing back the heat.

blocks.text: If you want Southern seafood by the sea

blocks.html: Head out toward the Sikao–Kantang–Hat Samran coast and you'll find seafood cooked the Southern way — crab curry with wild betel leaf, crab stir-fried in curry powder, and stink bean with fresh-off-the-boat seafood, often better value than in town.

items.name: Pak Meng Seafood (Sikao)
items.blurb: A seafood spot around Pak Meng Beach, known for two-water grouper, stir-fried squid and grilled shrimp, cooked with well-balanced Southern flavours, with a view close to the sea.

items.name: Ton Por House (Hat Samran)
items.blurb: A roadside place around Hat Samran, known for crab roe curry and deep-fried soft-shell crab, with friendly prices. A handy stop on the way down to the Southern coast.

items.name: Ja Nai Seafood (Koh Libong)
items.blurb: A spot on Koh Libong known for squid stir-fried in its own ink, sea-urchin curry, and fish straight from the sea. Good if you're heading to Libong to see the dugongs.

blocks.title: Worth knowing before you go
blocks.html: A lot of rice-curry shops and home-style places only open until afternoon or early evening, and some take a day off each week (Jeen Dam closes Saturdays · Krua Thong Na Tham closes the second Wednesday of the month). Checking before you set out is the safer bet. For seafood by the sea, go late morning to afternoon for the freshest catch and a table with a view.

blocks.text: Making the most of Southern Trang in a day

blocks.html: If you've got a single day in Trang town and want to taste the full range of Southern food, here's an order that's easy on the stomach and won't leave you stuffed.

items: Morning — start light with dim sum and old-style coffee at an in-town shop, before the bold stuff.
Lunch — dig into Southern rice-curry; pick gaeng tai pla, khua kling and stink-bean stir-fry on one plate.
Afternoon — rest the palate with pak liang and egg, or coffee at a café in the old-town area.
Evening — finish with Southern seafood by the sea around Pak Meng if you've got a car, or a made-to-order spot in town.

faq.q: Is Southern food in Trang very spicy for people not used to it?
faq.a: It's noticeably hotter and bolder than central-Thai food, especially gaeng tai pla, which leads with salt and runs hot. Tell the shop you want it mild and order pak noah (fresh veg on the side) to cut the heat. Khua kling and stink-bean stir-fry are easier to adjust down.

faq.q: Which Southern restaurants in Trang do locals actually go to?
faq.a: The ones locals mention most are Krua Khon Trang and Sifa Lifestyle Food in town, the old-school Ko Choi, Jeen Dam out in Huai Yot, and Krua Thong Na Tham out of town. All of them serve gaeng tai pla, khua kling and stink-bean stir-fry the traditional way.

faq.q: What is gaeng tai pla, and why do Southerners love it?
faq.a: It's an intense curry built on tai pla — fermented, salted fish innards — with grilled fish, bamboo shoots and vegetables. Salty and very spicy, eaten with steamed rice and fresh veg on the side. It's the dish that says 'real Southern food' more clearly than any other.

faq.q: Where's a good place to eat stink-bean stir-fry in Trang?
faq.a: Stink-bean stir-fry with shrimp paste and fresh shrimp is on the menu at nearly every Southern restaurant in Trang. The ones reviewers praise often are Ko Choi, Jeen Dam and Krua Mueang Trang. If you want it with fresh sea shrimp, try a seafood spot around Pak Meng or Hat Samran.

faq.q: How late do Southern rice-curry shops in Trang stay open?
faq.a: Most open from morning until afternoon or early evening, and the good curries often sell out by lunch. Go before 2pm to get the full range, and check each shop's weekly day off before you head out.
